items.title: 43 Highway Closures Hit Peel Region's Busiest Routes on August 7
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 43 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 7, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, six of the busiest corridors linking Mississauga to the rest of the Greater Toronto Area. Mississauga.com reports the closures are tied to short-term and emergency repairs and general maintenance work rather than one large construction project. With so many highways affected on the same day, drivers are advised to plan their trip before heading out rather than assume their usual route will be clear. The outlet also points to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region. Commuters passing through the region on Friday should expect at least some detours or lane restrictions as crews work through the scheduled repairs.

items.title: The Officer Who Ran Onto a Burning Plane at Pearson Is Getting a Street Named After Him
items.summary: According to INsauga, a street dedication ceremony this month will honour retired Sgt. Lonsdale “Lonny” Blackett, who became the first Black police officer in Brampton and Mississauga after joining Peel Regional Police's very first recruiting class in 1974. He was one of two Black recruits in that class and the only one to complete training, going on to a 33-year career during which he faced racism both on and off the force before eventually becoming a recruiter who helped bring in other minority officers. Blackett also helped found the Peel Regional Police Airport Division, and INsauga reports he was one of the officers who ran onto the burning wreckage of Air France Flight 358 to help evacuate people after it crashed at Pearson International Airport in 2005. All 309 passengers and crew aboard survived, and Blackett received a commendation for his role in the rescue. The City of Brampton began the process of naming a street after him in February, and the upcoming ceremony will mark the future site of Lonsdale Blackett Way at Mississauga Road just south of Bovaird Drive West. Since the street itself has not been built yet as part of planned development in the area, the city says the event will be a ceremonial dedication rather than an unveiling of a finished road. Residents are invited to attend, though the city notes parking will be limited.

items.title: After a Burst Pipe and a Food Truck Detour, Pal' Antojo Finally Opens on Queen Street
items.summary: According to INsauga, Pal' Antojo Mexican Restaurant has officially opened at 277 Queen St. S. in Mississauga, taking over a space that Border MX Mexican Grill quietly vacated late last year. Border MX had operated there since 2014 and built a following for its open-air patio, live music nights and mix of traditional and modern Mexican dishes, but the business hit trouble after a pipe burst inside the restaurant on Valentine's Day 2025, causing major water damage to the kitchen. INsauga reports the restaurant reopened that April before eventually closing for good. Pal' Antojo said in May that it was preparing the same Queen Street location to open, running a food truck behind the building in the meantime to keep serving customers. The restaurant announced it was finally open with the message “The wait is over!” The opening gives the block a new tenant after months of uncertainty following Border MX's closure.

items.title: Detached Home Prices in Mississauga Post Their Steepest Monthly Drop of Any Property Type
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's housing market cooled further in July, with both sales and prices moving lower as buyers grew more cautious, based on Zoocasa's analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The average home price in June had been $1,014,120, while the July 2025 year-ago average sat at $995,599, giving a sense of how the market has shifted over the past year. Sales slipped to 500 transactions for the month, and the housing supply also pulled back, though homes that did sell still moved in an average of 47 days, matching June's pace, INsauga reports. Detached homes led the overall slowdown, with Zoocasa noting their average price fell about 2 per cent, from $1,482,130 in June to $1,256,800 in July, the steepest decline of any property type tracked. The broader cooling suggests Mississauga buyers are taking a more cautious approach to the market heading into late summer, even as homes that do sell continue to move at a steady pace.

items.title: Fake Tenants Helped Pull Off a $30,000 Rental Scam Across Mississauga, Police Say
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police's Fraud Bureau is seeking two suspects connected to an apartment rental scheme that police say victimized at least eight people in Mississauga. Investigators say the rental units were advertised on social media between January and February 2025, and prospective renters who came to view the apartments were met by people posing as current tenants. Victims went on to sign rental agreements online and sent payment by e-transfer to secure the units, only to discover on move-in day that the apartments were never actually available. INsauga reports the individuals who had posed as landlords became impossible to reach once the scheme unravelled. Police say the combined financial losses across the eight identified victims exceed $30,000, and none of them received either the promised housing or their money back. Warrants have now been issued for the arrest of two people in connection with the scheme.
